transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

The usual causes are simply that the tray has come off its centre drive, food debris is stopping the roller ring, or a large dish is catching. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Lift out the glass tray and roller ring. Clean the ring and the microwave floor underneath, and make sure all the little wheels on the ring turn freely.
2. Check the small plastic drive piece in the centre: it should not be split, rounded off or loose. Refit the roller ring and tray so the tray’s centre grooves engage with it. Also check that the dish you use is not rubbing the sides.
3. Then run it with a cup of water for a minute. If it turns again, it was a seating, dirt or obstruction issue. If it still does not turn, note whether you can hear a faint motor hum/attempt to turn beneath the tray: hum but no movement points more to the centre coupler; no sound or movement makes the turntable motor more likely. Do not remove the microwave casing or investigate internal parts: microwaves can retain dangerous high voltage even when unplugged.

ok did that. the plate sits on the middle bit but wobbles, roller ring is in and the wheels turn fine. ran it with a cup of water and the little 3 pronged plastic piece in the middle wobbles and doesnt really turn. also theres a faint grinding/clicking from the centre when it runs

This now points most strongly to the turntable coupler — the small three-pronged plastic drive piece — being worn or split. A loose coupler lets the plate wobble and can make a clicking/grinding sound as it slips. 1. Switch off and unplug the microwave. Lift out the glass plate and roller ring, then see whether the plastic coupler lifts straight up off its spindle. Inspect its underside and centre hole for a crack, rounded-off shape or looseness. - If it is visibly split or rounded, that is the likely failed part. - If it looks sound and fits firmly on the spindle, but still wobbles/clicks when used, the turntable motor/gearbox underneath is more likely. Do not remove the microwave casing to inspect the motor. Keep using a cup of water whenever testing it — never run a microwave empty. If the coupler proves sound, an engineer would need to diagnose or check the turntable motor; whether that is worthwhile depends on the microwave’s age and overall condition.
took the plate and ring out, the plastic piece has a crack in it and the hole in the middle looks rounded. its a Sharp R272WM if that helps

[Heading: Likely cause: turntable coupler]
The cracked, rounded turntable coupler is the clear cause of the plate wobbling and failing to turn. It is slipping on its spindle, which explains the clicking/grinding and the uneven heating. Replace the small three-pronged plastic turntable coupler only; no internal microwave work should be needed. Take the old one with you or match it carefully by its overall shape and the centre-hole/spindle fit. I could not confirm an exact parts match from the R272WM reference alone, so use Sharp’s official spares route or a reputable microwave-spares supplier rather than ordering purely by appearance. Once replaced, refit the roller ring and glass plate, then test with a cup of water. If the new coupler still does not rotate properly, the turntable motor/gearbox is likely also worn and that would need an engineer—do not remove the microwave casing yourself.
